category_title: Gifted Hispanic female underachieving due to perceived inadequacy and lack of task relevance
minimal_context: The tutor and student are reviewing written comments on an English essay during a one-on-one meeting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your essay, Jennifer. Please look over the written comments I left on it so you can revise it for the final draft.

STUDENT: Wait, you actually read my paper? I just figured you would put a grade on it and hand it back.

TUTOR: Yes, I read all the papers. What do you think about the feedback I wrote?

STUDENT: I mean, I got a 95 on it. I'm satisfied with my work as long as my grades are acceptable.

TUTOR: But you could elaborate more and extend your thinking. Don't you want to improve?

STUDENT: I don't see any advantage in making the additional effort to read and apply those comments. I already have a good grade, and I don't see any value in how this task is relevant to my life anyway.

options.A: Guide her through a healing-lake visualization, encouraging her to observe that the lake is always changing yet always itself.
options.B: Begin grading her essays with more rigor, since she is capable of producing work of a superior quality.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for her essay revisions and final drafts throughout the semester.
options.D: Require her to use Evernote to take notes, organize her writing, and archive past essays.
